chunks: Al-Saffar, from Ibrahim ibn Hashim, from Nuh ibn Shu'ayb, from Hariz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim or Zurarah, who said:
Salat (prayer) over the deceased after he is buried is only du'a (supplication).
He said: Then al-Najashi—the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم did not perform salat (prayer) over him? He said: No, he only supplicated for him.

And it is possible that the basis in the reports which include the permissibility of salat (prayer) over the grave is when it has not yet been covered with soil; then once it has been covered with soil, that is not permitted. This indicates that.

key_terms.التُّرَابِ: the soil covering the deceased, marking the point after which the ruling changes
key_terms.الدُّعَاءُ: supplication, as distinct from the formal funeral salat (prayer)
key_terms.الصَّلَاةُ: the funeral salat (prayer) being discussed in legal context
key_terms.النَّجَاشِيُّ: al-Najashi, mentioned as an example in the discussion
key_terms.الْقَبْرِ: the grave, in relation to whether salat (prayer) may be performed at it
key_terms.الْمَيِّتِ: the deceased person over whom the prayer or supplication is made

ai.seo_question: Is salat (prayer) over a deceased person allowed after burial in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This text discusses the ruling of salat (prayer) over the deceased after burial, stating that what remains after burial is only du'a (supplication), not the formal funeral prayer. It also distinguishes reports about praying at the grave by suggesting they apply before the grave is fully covered with soil.
